subject: SIG/CAIQ: subprocessor fingerprints, telemetry & escrow clarifications
messages:
From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@novagrid.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: SIG/CAIQ follow-up - subprocessor fingerprints & telemetry questions

Kimberly,

Thanks again for taking this. As we progress through your SIG/CAIQ, a few clarifications on third-party runtime dependencies would help us close the review faster. Please see the asks below — target for completion EOD Dec 3 if possible.

1) Cryptographic custody/residency: for each KMS/subprocessor that touches encryption keys (customer or platform), can you confirm the residency (US/EU/APAC), and whether keys are customer-managed vs Redwood-managed? We need the provider name and the representative data center region.

2) Subprocessor fingerprints: for model artifacts and runtime binaries used in production, please provide a short mapping: provider, artifact type, and a stable fingerprint (SHA256) or build identifier we can reference. A single CSV is fine.

3) Telemetry retention & access: runtime traces, aggregated metrics, and request logs — retention windows and whether traces contain customer PII (yes/no). If different by region, flag that.

4) Escrow / SBOM plan: does Redwood have an escrow arrangement or SBOM for runtime components that we can reference? If not, what is the planned cadence to provide SBOMs to customers under NDA?

5) On-call & proofs: a simple on-call matrix for subprocessors (primary, secondary, SLA hours) helps our operations team.

Deliverables can be attachments or a shared Drive link. If you need a template, we can provide our subprocessor workbook.

Appreciate it — Alex

--
Alex Taylor
Senior Security Engineer, Novagrid Health
security@novagrid.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@novagrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up - subprocessor fingerprints & telemetry questions

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Marissa (security ops) and Jonas (runtime lead) are looped in. We can provide the items you requested; below is our delivery plan and a few clarifying Qs.

Planned deliverables (attached):
- subprocessors_fingerprint_list.csv: mapping of runtime providers and SHA256-style fingerprints or build IDs
- telemetry_retention_matrix.pdf: retention windows by data class and region
- oncall_matrix.xlsx: primary/secondary contacts and SLA coverage (non-sensitive contact IDs)

Clarifying items for you:
- For "fingerprints" we capture both package/binary signatures (for curated runtime images) and model artifact hashes where available. If you prefer only cryptographic hashes for deployed model binaries, say so and we'll narrow.
- Escrow/SBOM: we maintain SBOMs for the runtime container images and can provide an NDA-protected bundle. We do not use a third-party code escrow by default; we offer an escrow path for enterprise customers under contract.

Timeline: initial bundle attached here; follow-up for EU residency specifics by EOD Dec 3 (Jonas will confirm region-by-provider).

Attachments: subprocessors_fingerprint_list.csv (preview), telemetry_retention_matrix.pdf (summary), oncall_matrix.xlsx (redacted contacts).

If that works I'll upload the full artifacts to the Drive folder and open TICKET-9832 for any redlines you raise.

Best,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@novagrid.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up - subprocessor fingerprints & telemetry questions

Kimberly — thanks for the quick plan and the preview attachments. One small add: for the KMS entries can you include whether key material ever leaves the HSM boundary (even transiently) and the jurisdiction of the HSM (e.g., us-east-1, eu-west-1)? That helps our legal team with residency mapping.

If Jonas can add that to the provider row in subprocessors_fingerprint_list.csv that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — Alex

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@novagrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T17:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up - subprocessor fingerprints & telemetry questions

Alex — delivered. Attached are the artifact stubs we discussed and a link to the full, NDA-protected Drive bundle: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleLink

Summary of what we uploaded to the folder:
- subprocessors_fingerprint_list.csv (provider, artifact type, SHA256/build-id, KMS HSM jurisdiction, key custody flag)
- telemetry_retention_matrix.pdf (metrics/traces/logs retention by region; PII flag per stream)
- oncall_matrix.xlsx (primary, secondary, SLA hours; redacted personal emails)
- SBOM_package_bundle.tar.gz (SBOMs for runtime images; access restricted under NDA)

Notes:
- KMS custody: where keys are customer-managed we note it explicitly; where Redwood manages keys we include the HSM region (us-east-1/eu-west-1) and whether key material leaves the HSM (no for our managed providers).
- Escrow/SBOM: SBOMs are in the folder under "SBOMs/". We have an enterprise escrow offer if you require a third-party escrow holder — we can provide contract language and an example agreement.

Next steps: I'll leave Jonas to confirm any provider-level residency exceptions by Monday; I've opened TICKET-9832 so we can track outstanding items and redlines. If you'd like a short sync (15-min) to walk through the folder let me know a time.

Thanks,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachments: subprocessors_fingerprint_list.csv, telemetry_retention_matrix.pdf, oncall_matrix.xlsx, SBOM_package_bundle.tar.gz
